record.context_brief: Conformal matings in the transcendental setting
record.original_question: Can one develop an obstruction theory and identify structural conditions under which a transcendental map with a Herman ring can be conformally mated with the action of a Fuchsian group or a subgroup of PSL(2, Z) on the upper half-plane? More specifically, when can a topological mating between the map and the group action be defined, when can that topological mating be promoted to a conformal one, and what dynamical feature distinguishes the resulting correspondence map when the function has a Herman ring?

evidence.quote: A conformal mating is a construction that "glues" the Julia set of a function to the action of a Fuchsian group (or subgroup of PSL(2, Z)) on the upper half-plane, creating a single function that incorporates both behaviors consistently-conformally and dynamically.

Conformal mating in the transcendental setting is far less developed than in the polynomial or rational case. Hence, one can study to develop an obstruction theory and identify structural conditions under which such matings could theoretically exist. The goal should be to determine when a topological mating between the map with a Herman ring and the group action can be defined, and whether such a topological mating can be promoted to a conformal one. What distinguishes the correspondence map whenever the function has a Herman ring?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let f : C → C be a transcendental meromorphic (or entire) function whose Fatou set contains a Herman ring, that is, a doubly connected periodic Fatou component on which an iterate of f is conformally conjugate to an irrational rotation of a round annulus {1 < |z| < r}. Let Γ be a Fuchsian group acting on the upper half-plane H by Möbius transformations; an important case is Γ a finite-index subgroup of PSL(2, Z). The Julia set J(f) ⊂ C carries the dynamics of f; the limit set Λ(Γ) ⊂ ∂H carries the dynamics of Γ.

A topological mating of (f, Γ) is, informally, a continuous dynamical system on a topological sphere (or appropriate quotient space) obtained by gluing the filled-in dynamical plane of f to a fundamental domain for Γ along boundary identifications that conjugate the boundary behavior of f to the action of Γ on its limit set, so that the resulting space supports a single continuous map combining the two dynamics. A conformal mating is a topological mating that can be realized so that the resulting map is holomorphic (or more generally a holomorphic correspondence) on a Riemann surface compatible with the gluing, with the conformal structures on the two pieces matching.

Problem. Develop an obstruction theory for the existence of conformal matings of transcendental maps with Herman rings and Fuchsian group actions. Specifically, address each of the following.

1. Existence of a topological mating. Identify necessary and sufficient structural conditions on f (with a Herman ring) and on Γ (a Fuchsian group, or a subgroup of PSL(2, Z)) under which a topological mating of f with the action of Γ on H can be defined. Make precise the boundary-gluing equivalence relation required, taking into account the transcendental nature of f (e.g. essential singularities, infinite-degree behavior, escaping set).

2. Promotion to a conformal mating. Determine when a topological mating, if it exists, can be promoted to a conformal one. Formulate and prove the analogue, in this transcendental setting, of obstruction-theoretic criteria (in the spirit of Thurston-type obstructions or Levy/Rees-Shishikura-Tan obstructions known for rational matings), adapted to the presence of a Herman ring and to the infinite-degree, non-compact features of transcendental dynamics.

3. Dynamical signature of the Herman ring. Identify a precise dynamical feature of the resulting holomorphic correspondence (or mated map) that distinguishes the case in which f possesses a Herman ring from the case in which it does not. In particular, characterize the image and behavior of the Herman ring under the mating construction within the correspondence dynamics.

Provide rigorous definitions, theorems with hypotheses, and proofs (or counterexamples) for each of (1)–(3).
artifact.status_search_result: Conformal mating in the transcendental setting, particularly involving maps with Herman rings and Fuchsian groups, is a recognized underdeveloped area. While conformal matings have been intensively studied for polynomials and rational maps (Bullett–Penrose, Bullett–Lomonaco, etc., and recent work on antiholomorphic matings), no general obstruction theory or existence result is known for transcendental maps with Herman rings mated with Fuchsian group actions. The problem, as posed, appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Mating quadratic maps with the modular group (Bullett–Lomonaco)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops conformal matings between quadratic rational maps and PSL(2,Z), in the rational (not transcendental) setting.
status_evidence.claim: Conformal mating theory is well developed in rational cases but the transcendental analogue remains undeveloped.

status_evidence.title: Herman rings of elliptic functions and transcendental dynamics surveys
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys of transcendental dynamics list Herman rings and matings as open directions, with no general obstruction theory available.
status_evidence.claim: No published general framework exists for mating transcendental maps with Herman rings to Fuchsian groups.
